original_question: For the same finite-interval Korteweg-de Vries problem u_t+u_x+u_{xxx}+u u_x=0 on 0<x<L, t>0, with initial data u(x,0)=phi(x) and boundary condition B_k u=~h taken from the four operator families B_1, B_2, B_3, B_4 described above, is the initial-boundary value problem well-posed in the negative-regularity regime H^s(0,L) for some s<=-1? The review notes that the known local theory reaches s>=0, can be extended to -1<s<=0, and conjectures that the bounded-interval problem is ill-posed for every s<-1.
target_in_paper: Section 4, the unnumbered open problem stated immediately after equation (4.18): "Is the IBVP well-posed in the space H^s(0,L) for some s\le -1?" together with the next sentence conjecturing that the IBVP (4.18) is ill-posed for every s<-1.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the bounded-interval KdV equation u_t+u_x+u_{xxx}+uu_x=0 on 0<x<L, the initial datum u(x,0)=phi(x), the negative-regularity threshold s\le -1, the paper’s statement that the known local theory reaches the nonnegative Sobolev regime and can be pushed into -1<s\le 0, and the authors’ conjectural expectation of ill-posedness for every s<-1.
missing_details: The paper’s actual open problem is posed for the specific IBVP labeled (4.18), i.e. the standard bounded-interval problem with three boundary traces u(0,t)=h_1(t), u(L,t)=h_2(t), and u_x(L,t)=h_3(t), not for the earlier general boundary-operator setting B_i u=h_i with arbitrary coefficient families.
The question is about local well-posedness in H^s(0,L), not the separate global well-posedness problem discussed just before it in the same section.
The quantifier is existential: does there exist some Sobolev index s\le -1 for which the IBVP is well-posed?
The conjecture in the paper is strictly for s<-1; the endpoint s=-1 is not resolved by that conjectural sentence and should not be collapsed into the same claim.
To be stand-alone, the problem should specify that L>0 is fixed and that the PDE is posed on a bounded interval (0,L) for t>0 (or on (0,L)\times(0,T) in local form).
The paper tacitly keeps the boundary data in the same sharp temporal trace spaces used in the established local theory for this IBVP; your draft omits that background requirement.
Your phrase "taken from the four operator families B_1, B_2, B_3, B_4 described above" is not paper-faithful for this exact open problem and broadens it beyond the official formulation in Section 4.
The draft depends on prior context ("the same finite-interval problem", "described above") rather than restating the exact Section 4 problem in a stand-alone way.
refined_question:
For the bounded-interval Korteweg-de Vries initial-boundary value problem singled out in equation (4.18) of the paper, namely
u_t+u_x+u_{xxx}+u u_x=0 on (0,L)\times(0,T),
u(x,0)=\phi(x),
u(0,t)=h_1(t), u(L,t)=h_2(t), and u_x(L,t)=h_3(t),
with L>0 fixed and boundary data taken in the same sharp temporal trace spaces used in the known local theory, does there exist any Sobolev index s\le -1 for which the problem is locally well-posed in H^s(0,L)? More specifically, is the authors’ conjecture correct that this IBVP is ill-posed for every s<-1, leaving at most the endpoint s=-1 as a possible borderline case?
justification: The draft is targeting the second well-posedness open problem in Section 4, not a numbered conjecture in an earlier section. In this paper there is no relevant Conjecture 1.1/Proposition 1.2/Theorem 1.3 chain for this issue; the nearest official formulation is the unnumbered question after equation (4.18). The surrounding context in Section 4 states that the previously established theory gives local well-posedness for this IBVP in the nonnegative regime and can be extended to -1<s\le 0, then asks whether the IBVP is well-posed for some s\le -1, and immediately records the conjecture that it is ill-posed for every s<-1. The main correction needed is scope: your draft imports the earlier general boundary-operator framework, but the Section 4 open problem is phrased for the specific standard bounded-interval IBVP (4.18), the same one discussed earlier in Section 2 and then revisited in Section 4.1 through the three boundary traces h_1, h_2, h_3.
